rows.note: This is the all-purpose word, used for organisms and metaphorically for people who live off others.

example.english: A parasite can live on another organism and survive by absorbing nutrients.
example.traditional: 寄生蟲可以寄生喺其他生物身上，靠吸收養分生存。
example.jyutping: gei3 sang1 cung4 ho2 ji5 gei3 saang1 hai2 kei4 taa1 sang1 mat6 san1 soeng6 kaau3 kap1 sau1 joeng5 fan6 sang1 cyun4

rows.note: Use this colloquial term for a person who idles and lives off their family or others, rather than for an animal parasite.

example.english: They stay at home all day doing nothing and live off their family—they’re really a parasite.
example.traditional: 佢成日匿喺屋企唔做嘢，靠屋企人養，真係個米蟲。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 nik1 hai2 uk1 kei2 m4 zou6 je5 kaau3 uk1 kei2 jan4 joeng5 zan1 hai6 go3 mai5 cung4

rows.note: Use this for a person, especially a man, financially supported by a romantic partner or woman.

example.english: They always rely on their girlfriend to support them financially; they’re really a parasite.
example.traditional: 佢成日靠女朋友畀錢養住，真係個食軟飯嘅人。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 kaau3 neoi5 pang4 jau5 bei2 cin2 joeng5 zyu6 zan1 hai6 go3 sik6 jyun5 faan6 ge3 jan4
